summary: Lemma4.8's pure-power cusp decay is incompatible with the actual homogeneous forcing; a resonant logarithm is unavoidable. The central obstruction construction is affected. A separate complex-phase map error is locally repairable. The main degeneration theorem is not disproved or certified.

problems.title: Resonant forcing rules out the pure-power bound in Lemma4.8
problems.claim: A solution of L_infinity vhat=uhat has |V|+eta|V'|+eta^2|V''|=O(eta^(n+1)) at the cusp endpoint.
assumptions_checked: Actual operator L=(1/(n+1))D_n+R, with R bounded by eta^(n+1) times the weighted two-derivative norm.
U=uhat(1-eta) is the paper's positive homogeneous solution, with opposite endpoint value1 and U=O(eta^(n+1)).
Scaled interior ODE estimates and Euler variation give U=A eta^(n+1)+O(eta^(2n+2)); a Volterra uniqueness argument proves A>0.
The contradiction assumes exactly equation4.38, so R V=O(eta^(2n+2)); no arbitrary model-only forcing is substituted.
The application has n=2; endpoint eta approaches0 inside the specified interval.
problems.decisive_check: For m=n+1 and V=eta^m W, (eta^(m+2)W')'=mA eta^m+O(eta^(2m)). Bounded W removes the growing branch but forces W=(mA/(m+1))log eta+C+O(eta^m), contradicting boundedness. In dimension2, V has leading (3A/4)eta^3 log eta.
problems.failed_step: The proposed -C1 eta^m+C2 eta^(2m) barrier has L-image O(eta^(2m)), not a positive constant, and cannot dominate U~A eta^m on any endpoint interval.
problems.core_dependency: Definition4.9/Lemma4.10 pp611-613 -> Proposition4.2 pairing p614 -> Theorem4.12 p615 and obstruction elimination p621 -> projected forcing/gradient equations5.13/5.18 p623, Claim5.3 p625 -> Theorem5.4 p626 -> Main Theorem deduction p628.
problems.impact_rationale: Major because an impossible central auxiliary bound damages the uniform obstruction construction and propagated proof estimates. Severity is not based on repair length. No counterexample to the main metric degeneration is claimed.
problems.repair_candidate: Allow eta^(n+1)(1+|log eta|) with weighted derivatives; reconstruct cutoffs, uniform obstruction estimates, weighted pairings, projection bounds and nonlinear iteration.
problems.repair_verified: Only the forced local logarithmic coefficient and failure of the printed barrier are established. Adding a homogeneous solution cannot remove the log.
problems.repair_boundary: Global inhomogeneous existence/sign/left Neumann condition after correction, all uniform constants and the complete gluing theorem remain unverified.
counterevidence: The negative logarithmic leading term is consistent with vhat<=0.
Several weighted logarithmic integrals remain finite; small power losses might absorb logs, so a full repair may be possible.
The main theorem is neither refuted nor accepted by this initial review.

paper.title: A Continuous Cusp Closing Process for Negative Kähler-Einstein Metrics
paper.authors: Xin Fu; Hans-Joachim Hein; Xumin Jiang
paper.version: Exact acquired source version and hashes will be bound by the6Pro source manifest before dependent review.

independent_acceptance.scope: Focused verification of the existing findings; no new whole-paper review

issue_results.exact_source: Printed p610, physical69, Lemma 4.8 equation (4.38) requires L_infinity vhat=uhat and |V|+eta|V'|+eta^2|V''|=O(eta^(n+1)). Definitions and hypotheses checked at physical29,62,64,66; n=2 in the application.
issue_results.independent_derivation: Put m=n+1. The actual relative-coefficient remainder obeys |R f|<=C eta^m(|f|+eta|f'|+eta^2|f''|), and L=(1/m)D+R with D=eta^2 d2-(m-2)eta d-m. Its roots are m and -1. The actual U=uhat(1-eta) is positive, nonzero and O(eta^m); rescaled interior ODE estimates give its two weighted derivative bounds. Therefore D U=O(eta^(2m)). D(eta^m Z)=(eta^(m+2)Z')' gives U=A eta^m+O(eta^(2m)). If A=0, the two vanishing integration constants and the remainder bound give M(r)<=C r^m M(r), forcing U=0 near zero and then everywhere by uniqueness. Hence A>0.
issue_results.decisive_contradiction: Assuming the claimed weighted pure-power bound for V gives D V=m A eta^m+O(eta^(2m)). With V=eta^m W, integration yields W'=C eta^(-m-2)+m A/(m+1) eta^(-1)+O(eta^(m-1)). Bounded W excludes the growing branch but leaves W=m A/(m+1)log eta+C0+O(eta^m), impossible. In dimension2 the forced term is (3A/4)eta^3 log eta.
issue_results.failed_step: The printed lower barrier -C1 eta^m+C2 eta^(2m) has model image (2m+1)C2 eta^(2m) and actual image O(eta^(2m)). It cannot dominate the actual forcing A eta^m on an interval reaching eta=0; the asserted positive constant bound drops a vanishing power.
issue_results.boundary_and_counterevidence: The logarithmic term has the desired negative sign and is compatible with boundedness and decay to zero. Adding a homogeneous solution changes a pure-power coefficient and cannot cancel resonance. The opposite-end Neumann adjustment therefore does not remove the contradiction. Some weighted logarithms remain integrable and small power losses may permit a repair; neither repairs all uniform estimates by itself.
issue_results.core_dependency: Read Definition4.9 and Lemma4.10 (physical70), direct use of (4.38) in Lemma4.10 (72), dominated convergence bound in Proposition4.2 (73), uniform inverse Theorem4.12 (74), explicit use of Proposition4.2 to kill the limiting obstruction (80), projected forcing and gradient bounds (82), Claim5.3 pairing (84), Theorem5.4 (85), and deduction of the Main Theorem (87). These are actual central dependencies, not merely parallel background lemmas.
issue_results.severity_and_repair_scope: Major because an impossible auxiliary estimate is used in the central uniform obstruction construction and later projection estimates. Whole-paper failure is not a condition for this severity. Only the local contradiction and required logarithmic behavior are established; global corrected existence, uniform constants, nonlinear iteration and the main metric theorem are not certified or refuted.

issue_results.exact_source: Physical8-9, printed549-550, Lemma2.3, Definition2.4 (2.17), and Lemma2.5 (2.18)-(2.20). Physical2-3 establish the complex-parameter family and main theorem scope.
issue_results.independent_derivation: For lambda=sigma^(-1/3), the defined composition is lambda^(-1)Phi(lambda z); expanding conjugate(lambda z)^2 gives the coefficient lambda^(-1)conjugate(lambda)^2 nu(lambda z), not lambda nu(lambda z).
issue_results.admissible_witness: Let sigma=i rho, rho>0 arbitrarily small, lambda=rho^(-1/3)exp(-i pi/6), and z=(r,-r,0) with fixed r>0. Then F(z)=0 and |lambda z|>R. Choose the small positive root a of 6r^2 a-2a^3=rho. With L=rho^(-1/3), q=a/(L r^2), the base cubic equals 6qL^4r^4-2q^3L^6r^6=1; q tends to the small implicit-function branch nu(lambda z). The composition yields (r+ia,-r+ia,0) and cubic i rho. The printed formula yields shifts a exp(-i pi/6) and has real cubic part 3sqrt(3)r^2 a>0, outside TY_(i rho).
issue_results.repair_and_boundary: The corrected coefficient has magnitude |lambda|. The real-coordinate chain rule gives derivatives bounded by C_k |lambda|^(k+1)|lambda z|^(-4-k)=C_k |sigma||z|^(-4-k). Cube-root equivariance and uniqueness of the small branch preserve the corrected composition. The positive-real subcase agrees with the print but does not cover the complex theorem.
issue_results.severity_and_dependency: Minor applies to the expanded formula because the original defining composition already supplies the valid geometric identification and the required derivative norms are reconstructed. No claim is made that all later coordinate calculations have independently been checked.
